 Discount or rebate back the monthly fee for months Wave does well on CC fees…. There are months they’ve made $$$$’s off us in CC fees. They could have a program to rebate back the monthly fee whenever CC fees exceed $150 or $250 for example.

reviews.text:
Finally retired Quickbooks. Hallelujah. When a company forgets that it’s built on customers choosing your product willingly, and instead squeezes the life out of you because they think we can’t leave them, it’s time to take a stand. 

So I risked it all to try Wave for a year. I’m very happy I did. I’d give it a five-star rating if it weren’t for a couple key issues:

Security
No multi-factor authentication to protect our passwords. This is criminal negligence IMHO, and you have every right to walk away until they fix this MASSIVE SECURITY HOLE. We are entrusting access to our bank accounts, and all we have is a password to protect it. Not cool, Wave. 

Invoicing
No direct credit card payments. 
To invoice my customers I have to send them an email that they then pay. I’d rather do like I did with Square, and have them tap their card on my phone. Yes, we carry a secure card reader in our pockets. Let us use that to take payments! 

Ok, so if I have to do an email invoice, I’d like it to take fewer steps. This is minor, but the UI is a bit clunky. Again, look to Square for ideas on how much smoother it can be enter a transaction and get paid. 

Banking & Reconciling
Why do you lose the categorization when the money is deposited? You have the info from the invoice as to what accounts to credit. Shouldn’t the deposit also show those categories, and be able to follow a deposit back to the invoice(s) that it satisfied?

More transparency with matching transactions. It’s not always clear to me when a transaction was matched to the bank statement. This is especially true when there’s a transfer. I want to see both sides as the same transaction. Maybe this is just me.
